nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: Last job. Vane's throwing himself a gala tonight — champagne for the railway men, speeches about progress, the works. And in his study sits the ledger: every forged deed, every bribe, every crooked number, in his own tidy handwriting.

nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: That book goes to Marshal Reyes at the depot and Vane's finished — properly, legally, in ink. No locks shot off the truth this time. Well. One window latch.

nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: All eyes will be wherever the noise is. Which brings me to the noise.

nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: That golden statue of himself out front. Lasso it into the begonias, and I promise you every soul at that party — Vane loudest of all — will be busy grieving it for an hour.

nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: Then the begonias are getting something eternal. Everybody wins. Go — and Cole? Leave the place better than you found it. Minus one statue.

nodes.speaker: Doc Vega
nodes.text: Four words. See, THIS is why plans should be simple. Go make history boring again.
